title: The characteristic gluing problem for the Einstein vacuum equations. Linear and non-linear analysis
authors: Stefanos Aretakis, Stefan Czimek, Igor Rodnianski
journal_status: no journal-ref on arXiv v1 page as accessed 2026-10-28; publication status not verified
relevance: Primary lead. Solves the codimension-10 null gluing near Minkowski. Regularity recorded from abstract: solution is C^{m+2} tangential and C^2 transversal to the null hypersurface (finite regularity, not smooth); higher-order gluing possible along bifurcated null hypersurfaces. 10-dim gauge-invariant conserved charges are the only obstructions; gauge-dependent charges matched by gauge transformations.
limits: Abstract page only this run. Vacuum only. Finite regularity means this result cannot be used where smooth matched data is required.
open_questions: Whether the charge obstructions reappear at higher regularity or in non-perturbative regimes

title: Obstruction-free gluing for the Einstein equations
read_depth: full-text (partial: abstract, introduction sec.1-1.1, and sec.2.3-2.6 including Thm 2.7, Thm 2.8, Thm 2.9, Def 2.12, Cor 2.13 extracted verbatim; secs. 3-6 and norm definitions sec.2.2 not read line-by-line)
journal_status: no journal-ref on arXiv v1 page as accessed 2026-10-28; publication status not verified
locator: Theorem 2.9 (main: obstruction-free null gluing); Corollary 2.13 (obstruction-free spacelike gluing); Definition 2.12 (asymptotic flatness g-e=O(r^-1), k=O(r^-2))
assumptions: Thm 2.9: sphere data x1 on S1 contained in ingoing null data xbar on a short incoming null hypersurface, satisfying null structure equations; sphere data x2 on S2; both close to Minkowski sphere data m in norms X, |xbar-m|+|x2-m| <= eps. Charge gaps between x2 and x1: Delta-E = C1*eps (strictly positive, of order eps), |Delta-L| <= C2*eps^2, and eps^{-1}Delta-E > C3(eps^{-1}|Delta-P| + eps^{-1}|Delta-G|) with C3 above a universal constant. Cor 2.13: asymptotically flat spacelike data (Def 2.12) with well-defined finite ADM parameters; Kerr target with Delta-E_ADM = C1 > 0, |Delta-L_ADM| <= C2, Delta-E_ADM > C3|Delta-P_ADM|, C3 > C-tilde_3; gluing across annulus A_[R,2R] far out in the asymptotic region, R > R-tilde.
conclusion: Thm 2.9: solution x of null structure equations along outgoing hypersurface with x|_{S2} = x2 EXACTLY and x|_{S1'} = x1' on a perturbed sphere (past-side data perturbed at O(eps) level), with high-frequency norm bound. Cor 2.13: data glued to chosen Kerr (or Schwarzschild of any mass M > M0) across the asymptotic annulus; obstructions (10 charges) removed by the nonlinearity, at the price of the charge-gap relation. No Regge-Teitelboim parity conditions needed (unlike Corvino-Schoen); only well-defined finite ADM L and center of mass.
proof_status: Proof not read this run (secs 3-6 unread); authors' claims recorded, theorem and corollary statements read verbatim from arXiv HTML v1.
relevance: Primary lead; the strongest published spacelike result for the genericity axis: obstructions removed in vacuum near Minkowski, but NOT unconditional (charge-gap conditions; perturbative; asymptotic annulus; target must be a chosen model family, not an arbitrary prescribed interior deformation).
limits: Vacuum only. Norm definitions (sec 2.2, Sobolev indices of X) not read: regularity class recorded only as the authors' X / X^{h.f.} spaces. Interior-annulus arbitrary deformations NOT covered; charge gap Delta-E = C1*eps > 0 strictly required, so exact charge matching to an arbitrary target is impossible within this theorem.
open_questions: Does the nonlinear (high-frequency) method remove the kernel obstruction for compact INTERIOR annuli with prescribed small source shift (our missing step M1)?
Extension to coupled Einstein-matter null constraints (our missing step M2): nothing found

title: Localized deformation for initial data sets with the dominant energy condition
read_depth: full-text (partial: abstract, sec.1 all four theorems and surrounding discussion, sec.2.1-2.3 including Prop 2.1, Prop 2.2, Def 2.3, Example 2.4 extracted verbatim; secs. 3-6 proofs not read)
version: arXiv:1606.03078v2 (10 Feb 2020; v1 9 Jun 2016); published Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations, DOI 10.1007/s00526-019-1679-9
locator: Thm 1.1 (localized deformation, C^{4,alpha} x C^{3,alpha}, no-kernel, weak->strict DEC); Thm 1.2 (higher regularity uniform version, smooth if data smooth); Thm 1.3 (interpolation gluing of two nearby data sets, DEC interpolates); Thm 1.4 (asymptotic gluing to admissible family incl. Kerr and Kerr-Newman, WITHOUT no-kernel assumption, ADM energy raised E_theta > E by controlled small amount, exact equality in B_R and outside B_{2R}); modified constraint map Phi^W (2.3); Example 2.4 (10-dim kernel of adjoint at flat data: K0 = span{1,x1,x2,x3}, K1 = translations and rotations)
assumptions: Initial data set (g,pi) in C^{k+4,alpha} x C^{k+3,alpha} on compact Omega-bar with boundary; kernel of DPhi^0_{(g,pi)}^* trivial on Omega (no-kernel condition) for Thm 1.1-1.3. Thm 1.4: asymptotically flat, NO kernel condition; finite-dimensional approximate kernel handled by admissible family. n >= 3.
conclusion: Compactly supported deformations (h,w) in C_c^{k+2,alpha} achieving mu_bar - |J_bar|_{g_bar} >= mu - |J+V|_g + psi: DEC INEQUALITY, not constraint equality. Authors' own remark (sec.1, after Thm 1.4): the gluing does NOT recover vacuum gluing because equality of the DEC is not obtained. Smooth output from smooth input. Admissible family can include non-vacuum model families such as Kerr-Newman.
proof_status: Proofs (secs 3-6) not read this run; theorem statements and abstract/introduction read verbatim from arXiv HTML v2.
relevance: Primary lead and the deep-read anchor of this lane. Establishes exactly the axis DEC-vs-fixed-matter: DEC-inequality deformations exist under no-kernel or via admissible families, but cannot deliver a FIXED matter model; explicit kill of any shortcut that would use DEC theorems for the coupled lemma.
limits: INEQUALITY only. Not usable for fixed coupled matter (mu,J must equal a prescribed field stress). Kernel-free condition fails at flat data (10-dim kernel, Ex. 2.4) and near symmetric regions.
open_questions: Whether the no-kernel condition in the interior can be removed by Czimek-Rodnianski/Mao-Oh-Tao flexibility methods (M1)
